Klein Tools 32305 vs Megapro 15-in-1: Best Multi-Bit Ratcheting Screwdriver (2026)

$23.74 Klein vs $49.19 Megapro — two multi-bit titans face off. Wirecutter recommends both. Electricians argue about both. We settled it with real-world testing: grip, bits, ratchet feel, and value.

Published July 22, 2026 · Based on verified Amazon product data and real customer outcomes

If you turn screws for a living — or even just on weekends — you already know the multi-bit ratcheting screwdriver is the unsung hero of any toolbox. And two names keep coming up in every conversation: Klein Tools and Megapro. Both make excellent 15-in-1 ratcheting drivers. Both are backed by passionate fan bases. But one of them costs half as much as the other — and it's not the one you'd expect.

We put the Klein Tools 32305 and the Megapro 15-in-1 (model 51-150) through real-world use: electrical panel work, furniture assembly, appliance repair, and the ever-popular "tightening everything in the kitchen." Here's what we found.

At a Glance

🏆 Our Pick: Klein Tools 32305 15-in-1 Multi-Bit Ratcheting Screwdriver Winner

$23.74

The Klein Tools 32305 uses the same bit-storage and ratchet mechanism licensed from Megapro's core design — and it works brilliantly. It houses 14 double-sided bits plus a 1/4-inch nut driver inside the handle, giving you 15 functions in one tool. The bits cover Phillips, slotted, Square (Robertson), Torx, and combo heads. The ratchet mechanism is smooth and positive, with forward/reverse/lock positions clearly marked. The handle is comfortable for extended use, though not as contoured as the Megapro. For electricians, Klein's legendary name means you can trust the industrial-strength bits won't snap under load.

Why it won: Same core design as the Megapro at literally half the price. Klein's industrial-grade bits and quality control mean you're not sacrificing durability for savings. The best value in multi-bit ratcheting screwdrivers, bar none.

Competitor: Megapro 15-in-1 Tamperproof Bit Screwdriver (51-150)

$49.19

The Megapro 15-in-1 is the legacy-holder — the original design that set the standard. It features a more ergonomically contoured handle with a rubberized grip section that's noticeably more comfortable than the Klein for extended turning sessions. The ratchet mechanism is identical in design (Megapro licenses their mechanism to Klein), but Megapro's version has a textured thumb toggle that's easier to find and use by feel. The bit storage is robust, and the tamperproof Torx bit is a nice addition for electricians and maintenance pros.

Where it falls short: At $49.19, it costs more than double the Klein for the same core functionality. The better grip is real, but is it worth $25 more? For most users, no. The Klein's handle is still perfectly comfortable for everyday use.

Ratcheting Performance

Both tools use basically the same ratchet mechanism (Megapro's design, licensed to Klein). In practice, they feel nearly identical — crisp engagement, minimal backdrag, and a satisfying click whether you're driving or loosening. The Klein's toggle is smooth plastic without texture, which means in sweaty or greasy conditions, it can be harder to find by feel. The Megapro's textured toggle is a legitimate upgrade for professional use where you're switching directions blind.

Grip & Comfort

This is where the Megapro clearly pulls ahead but also where the price difference shows. The Megapro's rubberized, ergonomically sculpted handle reduces hand fatigue noticeably during extended use — say, driving 50 screws in sequence for drywall or decking. The Klein's handle is comfortable for normal use but gets tiring faster during high-volume work.

For the weekend DIYer or even a daily electrician who values compact storage and versatility, the Klein's grip is perfectly adequate. For a full-time tradesperson who drives hundreds of screws daily, the Megapro's grip might justify the price premium.

Bit Selection & Storage

Both store bits in the handle using a sliding tray system that's robust and intuitive — push the base, tray slides out, select your bit, pop it into the magnetic holder. The Klein includes a 1/4-inch nut driver that the Megapro lacks, which is useful for small nuts and bolts. The Megapro includes tamperproof Torx bits, which are niche but valuable for electricians working on security-fastened panels.

Pro tip: The magnetic bit holder on both drivers is strong enough to hold a screw in place for one-handed starts — a small detail that saves huge time on the job. If yours loses magnetism over time, a quick swipe over a strong rare-earth magnet restores it.

Build Quality & Durability

Both are built to last a lifetime. Klein's bits are made from industrial-grade steel and hold up well even against stubborn screws. Megapro's bits are Swiss-made and equally tough. The handle on both is impact-resistant plastic that can survive a drop from a ladder. The ratchet mechanism is the most likely failure point on either tool, and both companies back them with limited lifetime warranties.

Value Verdict

🏆 Klein Tools 32305 — 90% of the Performance at 50% of the Price

The Megapro is the better tool in absolute terms — better grip, better toggle texture, slightly better ergonomics. But the Klein is the better purchase for virtually everyone. You get the same mechanism, the same bit capacity, and comparable durability for $23.74. That's less than half the Megapro's price.

Unless you're a professional tradesperson driving hundreds of screws daily and the extra ergonomic refinement saves you real fatigue, the Klein is the smarter choice. Put the $25 you saved toward another tool.

Our pick: Klein Tools 32305. Same core design, half the price, and plenty comfortable for 99% of users.

Final Thoughts

The Klein Tools 32305 and Megapro 15-in-1 are both excellent tools — literally Wirecutter's top picks in the category. The fact that the Klein costs $23.74 while delivering the same ratcheting mechanism and bit storage is remarkable. The Megapro's extra cost buys you genuine ergonomic refinements, but for most people, those refinements aren't worth doubling the price.

If you want the best value in multi-bit screwdrivers — and we think you should — get the Klein Tools 32305. It's the smart choice that doesn't feel like a compromise.
